test "the client can read what the server declared, with the settings map intact" do
      {:ok, client} = Client.start_link(transport: {MockTransport, []})
      transport = Client.transport(client)

      extensions = %{
        "io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks" => %{},
        "com.example/thing" => %{"mimeTypes" => ["text/html"], "nested" => %{"depth" => 2}}
      }

      {result, _request} =
        discover(client, transport, %{"tools" => %{}, "extensions" => extensions})

      assert result.server_capabilities.extensions == extensions
      assert Client.server_capabilities(client).extensions == extensions

      # An extension we do not implement is neither rejected, nor rewritten,
      # nor reported as a fault — the posture `extensions.ex:56-61` commits to
      # in prose and nothing tested.
      assert get_in(result.server_capabilities.extensions, [
               "com.example/thing",
               "nested",
               "depth"
             ]) == 2
    end

counterfactual.reading: None can: the client MUST accept an SSE response (streamable-http.mdx:88-91) and reads it per the SSE specification the transport cites (:35, :151-153), under which each blank line dispatches the event before it, so one chunk holding two events yields `hello` then `world`.

counterfactual.question: could a conforming SDK fail this unit?

unit.docs/conformance/buckets/bucket-1-2026-0: the member: that view's unit is the member, so the question is asked of the member's whole test

counterfactual.grain_ruling: PM ruling 29717: the grain is WIRE MEANING. Two SDKs that give one wire state the same meaning in different host values are the same SDK here.
counterfactual.grain: Asked of the wire meaning the asserted value denotes, read as A2 gate 2 reads it (etcc-membership.md §2.2, §2.4).

incidental_traffic.rule: A reading fires when a conforming SDK's ASSERTED value could differ in form or meaning. It does not fire on incidental traffic: an extra or reordered request that trips the mock's message sequencing (a serialising SDK, or a re-fetch of a ttlMs: 0 result) is not an asserted value. Asked otherwise, every client test fires, the 29717 degeneracy one level down.

precedence.rule: redundant takes precedence: a member with a missed edge is routed to A3 and its reading is recorded honestly, firing or not.
